title: Sell Mineral Rights in Allison, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Allison, PA | Fayette County
metaDescription: Allison, PA mineral owners in Fayette's coal country: get a clear cash offer on your Marcellus royalty interest, no obligation.
heroLead: Allison sits in Fayette County's old coal-patch country, land that changed hands through coal companies long before anyone drilled for Marcellus gas.
intro: Fayette County's mineral history runs deep, and not only because of shale gas. This part of the state was coke and coal country for the better part of a century, and a lot of Allison-area families hold oil and gas rights today because a coal company only ever wanted the coal seam, leaving the deeper formations with the original landowner or whoever the family sold those rights to separately down the line. Untangling which rights your family actually still holds takes real title work, not guesswork.
We've done that kind of digging on our own family's deed before, and we'll do the same for yours before we ever discuss a number.

sections.heading: Coal severance and what it did, and didn't, take
paragraphs: A coal severance deed transfers rights to a specific coal seam, not automatically the oil, gas, or deeper mineral rights beneath it. If your family's Allison-area land was affected by a coal severance decades ago, there's a real chance the oil and gas rights, including whatever Marcellus or Utica potential exists underneath, stayed with your family the whole time.

This part of Fayette County has both legacy conventional oil and gas history from the shallower formations and more recent Marcellus and deeper Utica leasing activity, so it's worth checking both layers of your title.

sections.heading: What we look for in old coal-country deeds
paragraphs: We trace your chain of title through the Fayette County Recorder of Deeds, specifically checking what was severed, when, and to whom, so we can tell you with confidence exactly what oil and gas rights remain in your family's name today.

sections.heading: Turning old paperwork into a real number
paragraphs: Once ownership is confirmed, we check current leasing and production activity tied to your parcel and build an offer around what's actually there, not what an old deed vaguely implies.

faqs.question: My family sold coal rights generations ago. Do we still own the gas rights?
faqs.answer: Very possibly, since a coal severance typically covers only the coal seam. We'll confirm exactly what your family retained by tracing the deed history.

faqs.question: Is there active Marcellus drilling near Allison?
faqs.answer: Fayette County has both legacy conventional wells and more recent unconventional development. We'll check what's active specifically near your parcel.

faqs.question: How far back do you need to trace the title?
faqs.answer: As far as needed to reach a clean, unbroken chain, sometimes back to the original coal-era severance from the early or mid-1900s.
